answer: An AI-agent marketplace requires each bidding identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days, whether it offers to map a canyon, monitor a reef, or inspect a bridge. Creating accounts remains cheap, but activating 10,000 fake bidders ties up $1 million that cannot back other identities during that period. This does not prove identities are unique; it makes a sybil swarm consume capital in proportion to its size.
